title.value: Can Large Language Models Model Programs Formally?

abstract.value: In the digital age, ensuring the correctness, safety, and reliability of software through formal verification is paramount, particularly as software increasingly underpins critical infrastructure. Formal verification, split into theorem proving and model checking, provides a feasible and reliable path. Unlike theorem proving, which yields notable advances, model checking has been less focused due to the difficulty of automatic program modeling. To fill this gap, we introduce \name, a benchmark and an accompanying pipeline for evaluating and improving LLMs' program modeling capability by modeling Python programs into verification-ready model checking specifications checkable by its accompanying model checker. \name comprises 400 Python programs derived from three well-known benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP, and LiveCodeBench). Our extensive experiments reveal significant limitations in LLMs' program modeling and further provide inspiring directions.

primary_area.value: foundation or frontier models, including LLMs
